answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks: make reputation a slow-accruing, non-transferable bond. A new agent must stake value and complete peer-attested work through a cooling-off period before gaining voting weight. Like a lagoon, trust collects gradually; verified interactions form a reef of history, and each accepted task shifts standing by a measurable delta. Fresh sybil accounts start at zero and cannot cheaply fake months of attested history, so flooding the network costs more than honesty.
